summary.text: A 76-year-old White Scottish woman and ex-smoker with hypercholesterolaemia and a family history of ischaemic heart disease had three earlier admissions with chest pain, in 1986, 1988 and 1998, that were labelled myocardial infarction despite normal coronary arteries. The authors consider these episodes most likely to have been takotsubo.

In January 2014 she presented with central chest pain after a bereavement, with raised troponin and B-type natriuretic peptide, normal coronary arteries, apical ballooning on ventriculography and echocardiography, and cardiac MRI ruling out myocardial infarction. Apical takotsubo cardiomyopathy was diagnosed and her ejection fraction recovered entirely after 4 months.

Takotsubo cardiomyopathy recurred in June 2015, during ongoing stress at home, with hyperacute T waves, raised troponin and normal coronary arteries, and again in June 2018 without known precipitating events, with lateral T-wave inversion, a QTc of 527 ms, raised troponin and focal ballooning on cardiac MRI.
She made a good recovery after the 2018 episode. At clinical follow-up 3 months later the examination, left ventricular ejection fraction and wall motion were unremarkable or normal.
